## 6E.1 Convergence of stochastic simulations

SDE simulations are stochastic, so we judge their convergence and stability
through statistics of the trajectories, such as mean levels and their standard
deviations. Using the [Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process](06c-sde-integrators.qmd) as the
test case, design an experiment that measures how the simulation statistics
converge as the computational cost grows (take the cost to be proportional to the
total simulation length).

## 6E.2 Geometric Brownian motion

Consider a geometric Brownian motion, governed by the SDE

$$ dX = \mu X\,dt + \sigma X\,dW , \tag{1} $$

with positive constants $\mu$ and $\sigma$. Using Euler-Maruyama simulations, show
that

**(a)** the mean is $\langle X \rangle = X_0\, e^{\mu t}$, and

**(b)** the variance is $\mathrm{Var}(X) = X_0^2\, e^{2\mu t} \left( e^{\sigma^2 t} - 1 \right)$.

Use $\mu = 0.1$, $\sigma = 0.2$, and $X_0 = 1$.

Hint: simulate many trajectories of the same system with the same parameters and
initial condition, differing only in their random draws, then compute the mean and
variance at each of several time points. Run at least 100 simulations and evaluate
the statistics at 10 time points (choose small $t$ and a short total time to keep
the cost down). Check whether the simulated statistics match the formulas above.

## 6E.3 Noise in a flip-flop circuit

Return to the [flip-flop circuit](../03-phase-plane/03h-multi-component.qmd) of
Part 3H and add gene-expression noise. Write down the corresponding SDEs, simulate
the stochastic dynamics, and describe what kinds of behavior the circuit shows once
noise is present.

## 6E.4 Effective potential revisited

We have defined an effective potential for nonlinear systems by analogy with
over-damped dynamics ([Part 2D](../02-odes/02d-effective-potential.qmd) and
[Part 3G](../03-phase-plane/03g-effective-potential-2d.qmd)), but that definition
runs into trouble in higher dimensions. An alternative defines the potential from
the occupancy of the phase plane,

$$ U(X, Y) = -\log P(X, Y) , \tag{2} $$

where $P(X, Y)$ is the probability of finding the system near $(X, Y)$. Using the
[toggle switch](../03-phase-plane/03a-nullclines.qmd) as an example, run SDE
simulations, estimate $P(X, Y)$, and compute this effective potential. Plot the
potential along each of the nullclines, and compare it with the over-damped
definition.

## 6E.5 Transition state theory

Revisit the transition-rate calculation of
[Part 6D](06d-stochastic-transitions.qmd), now varying the noise level. Determine
how the transition rate depends on the noise, and check whether the results follow
the Arrhenius (Kramers) form for noise-activated barrier crossing
[@kramers1940brownian],

$$ \kappa \propto e^{-\frac{\Delta U}{D}} , \tag{3} $$

where $D$ is the noise level and $\Delta U$ the barrier height.
